test_title: PYST 6: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Electricity Plan 2023:

1. It projects over 50% installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.

2. It proposes nationwide shutdown of thermal plants older than 25 years.

Which of the following is/are Correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Electricity Plan 2023** projects over **50% of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources** by **2030**. This aligns with India’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions and its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The plan does not propose a **nationwide shutdown of thermal plants older than 25 years**. Instead, it suggests a phased retirement of these plants based on their efficiency and economic viability. The focus is on reducing emissions without compromising energy security. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• India aims to achieve an installed renewable energy capacity of **500 GW by 2030**, a target that aligns with the goals outlined in the National Electricity Plan 2023.
 
• The plan also highlights the importance of energy storage solutions, such as battery storage systems and pumped hydro storage, to address the intermittency of renewable energy sources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Electricity Plan:**

 
 
• The plan is prepared by the **Central Electricity Authority (CEA)** under the Ministry of Power every five years. It serves as a roadmap for the development of the power sector in India.
 
• It includes projections for demand, generation capacity, transmission infrastructure, and policy recommendations to meet future energy needs.
 
 
 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Goals:**
 
 
• India has pledged to achieve **50% of its installed energy capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030**.
 
• It also aims to reduce the emission intensity of its GDP by **33-35% from 2005 levels by 2030**.
 
• As of 2023, India’s total installed renewable energy capacity is over **170 GW**, including solar, wind, bio-energy, and small hydro.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Power Plants in India:**
 
 
• India has a significant number of coal-based thermal power plants, many of which are over 25 years old.
 
• Phasing out older, inefficient plants is a priority to reduce emissions and improve energy efficiency.
 
• However, thermal power remains a crucial part of India’s energy mix to ensure grid stability.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transition Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government has launched schemes like the **National Solar Mission** and **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy** to boost renewable energy adoption.
 
• India is also investing in advanced energy storage technologies and grid modernization to support renewable energy integration.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Commitments:**
 
 
• India’s commitments under the **Paris Agreement** include achieving net-zero carbon emissions by **2070**.
 
• The National Electricity Plan 2023 is a crucial step in meeting these international commitments while ensuring sustainable development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Demand:** India’s electricity demand is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of **6-7% by 2030**.
 
• **International Collaboration:** India is working with countries like the US and UK under initiatives like **Mission Innovation** and the **International Solar Alliance** to promote clean energy technologies.
 
• **Hydrogen Economy:** The government is also focusing on developing a **green hydrogen ecosystem** as a clean energy alternative.
 
• **Decarbonization:** The plan emphasizes the decarbonization of the power sector while maintaining energy security and affordability.
